questions.q: What does an Account represent in Salesforce?
options: A single person who works at a company
A single sales deal in progress
The company or organization a relationship is with
A customer support ticket
questions.explain: Account represents the company or organization itself. Contact represents a person tied to that Account.

questions.q: On the New Account form, which field is required to save by default?
options: Account Name
Industry
Billing Address
Annual Revenue
questions.explain: Account Name is the only field required to save a new Account by default; everything else on the form is optional detail.

questions.q: Looking at a Contact record's Related tab, what might you see tied directly to that person?
options: Only fields, never related records
A list of every Account in the org
Page layout XML
Opportunities and Cases tied specifically to that Contact
questions.explain: A Contact record's Related tab can show Opportunities and Cases tied to that specific person, not just records on the parent Account.

questions.q: What does the Contacts to Multiple Accounts feature allow?
options: A single Account to have two different names
A Contact to have indirect relationships to Accounts beyond its primary one
Two Contacts to share one email address
An Account to be deleted automatically after a Contact is removed
questions.explain: Contacts to Multiple Accounts, an optional feature, lets a Contact keep one primary (direct) Account while also having indirect relationships to other Accounts.

questions.q: Is Contacts to Multiple Accounts enabled by default in a new Salesforce org?
options: Yes, it's on for every org automatically
It only applies to Person Accounts
No, it's an optional feature an admin turns on
It replaces the standard Contact object entirely
questions.explain: Contacts to Multiple Accounts is off by default — an admin has to enable it for indirect Account relationships to appear.
